title: UMSF Bench Prototype: ESP32 sensor firmware and local monitoring interface

description:
Source code of the ESP32 bench prototype of the UMSF project (University of Customs and Finance, Dnipro): firmware of the gateway AG1 and of the wearable sensor nodes W01–W03, the local web monitoring interface served by the gateway, and documentation of the hardware, ESP-NOW packet formats and the HTTP API.

  • Gateway AG1: receives ESP-NOW broadcasts from fixed and wearable nodes, runs a Wi-Fi access point and serves a dashboard at http://192.168.4.1 that works without internet (personnel, structural monitoring, signs of life, situation assessment, event log, latched alarms with operator reset).
  • Wearable node: on-node heart-rate estimation from a MAX30102 PPG sensor (adaptive peak detection, motion gating, median of beat-to-beat intervals), impact/fall detection with an MPU-6050, skin temperature (DS18B20) and an SOS button. Simulated heart-rate values are flagged in every packet.
  • Interface simulator: a Python script that serves the unchanged dashboard with synthetic data, so the interface can be inspected without hardware.

This prototype motivated the record fields, event types and evidence states of UMSF Incident Lab (Appendix A of the accompanying software paper). It is archived for provenance and reuse. Readings are uncalibrated, the heart-rate algorithm is not validated against a reference device, and the prototype is neither a medical device nor a certified safety system. The fixed (structural) node firmware is not included in this version; its packet contract is documented.
notes: Bench prototype for provenance and reuse. All readings uncalibrated. The interface simulator uses synthetic data only.
